⚡ 8 Transformation Priorities

1. National Peat Depth Baseline

Complete UK peat depth mapping within 2 years. Ground-truthed by coring at 1km grid. Loss rate calculated against historical baselines. Priority mapping for degraded sites with high carbon loss.

2. Carbon Credit Integrity

Peatland Code compliance automated. Carbon stock verified by satellite + ground-truthing. No double-counting of carbon credits. Additionality assessment standardised. Verification audit trail maintained.

3. Hydrological Restoration Priority

Most hydrologically degraded sites identified first for restoration. Gully blocking and bund effectiveness measured. Water table recovery tracked in real-time. DOC reduction quantified per restoration intervention.

4. Fire Prevention Over Reaction

Peat fire risk index published daily during dry season. Controlled burn compliance monitoring. Community fire alerting system. Post-fire rapid assessment capability. Fire recovery tracking as standard.

5. Biodiversity Co-Benefit Tracking

Restoration sites assessed for biodiversity gains alongside carbon. Curlew/hen harrier habitat improvement measured. Invasive species control prioritised. Ecological condition as restoration success metric.

6. Grazing-Peat Balance

Stocking density recommendations based on peat condition science. Overgrazing thresholds mapped to peat loss rates. Common grazing rights respected while protecting peatland. Evidence-based moorland management agreements.

7. Satellite-Powered Continuous Monitoring

Sentinel-2 analysis at 10-day intervals for all UK peatlands. InSAR subsidence detection for drainage impact. Thermal anomaly alerting for fire risk. Cloud-free composite for vegetation health.

8. Parliamentary Peatland Accountability

Annual national peatland condition report. Restoration target progress dashboard. Carbon emission reduction metrics. Peatland Code market transparency. International benchmarking against Finland/Norway/Canada.

🚫 Red Lines (Never Crossed)

  • ❌ No peat extraction permitted on SSSI/SPA peatland — conservation designation overrides commercial interest
  • ❌ No carbon credit issued without ground-truth verification — satellite-only claims are insufficient
  • ❌ No controlled burn permitted without peatland fire risk assessment — moorland management science-based
  • ❌ No restoration site approved without hydrological impact assessment — water table recovery is the primary metric
  • ❌ No overgrazing threshold exceeded without mitigation plan — peat condition science dictates stocking density
  • ❌ No peatland data published at individual landowner level without consent — privacy protection for common grazing rights

🤝 5-Step Engagement Model

4

5
Assure: Continuous audit-grade peatland governance reporting. Carbon credit transparency. Parliamentary peatland condition evidence. Biodiversity co-benefit metrics.
